meta.subtitle: Q2 2026 10-Q: revenue +10% with 5% organic, margins up in every segment; the shares sit near their 52-week high at 26.2x FY26 consensus EPS

advisories: model vs Street expected return diverge by 37pp — informational, not scored

analystSentiment.commentary: We rate Thermo Fisher Scientific HOLD with a 12-month target range of $605 to $705 against a price of $658.92. The second quarter was good: revenue grew 10% to $11.99 billion, organic growth was 5%, adjusted EPS rose 13% to $6.03 and GAAP operating margin widened to 17.4%. The obstacle is the price. The shares sit just below their 52-week high of $671.47 after rising from a low of $435.27, the consensus target of $649.96 is below the current price, and the stock trades at 26.2x the FY26 consensus EPS of $25.13. Our Base values the shares a year out at about twenty-five times the FY27 consensus EPS of $27.54, a modest step down from today's forward multiple, for $688.50. The Bull, at $780.00, needs the multiple to expand to the Street's high target; the Bear, at $520.00, has earnings stall at the FY26 level and the multiple fall to about twenty-one times, the Street's low target. At weights of 25%, 50% and 25%, the probability-weighted value is $669.25, close to the price, while the Bear sits about a fifth below it. The label is HOLD because of where the price stands, not because the business has weakened.

executiveSummary.companyOverview: Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc., founded in 1956 and headquartered in Waltham, Massachusetts, sells life sciences solutions, analytical instruments, specialty diagnostics, and laboratory products and biopharma services. It reports four segments. Life Sciences Solutions supplies reagents, instruments and consumables for biological and medical research and for the discovery and production of drugs and vaccines. Analytical Instruments provides instruments, consumables, software and services to pharmaceutical, biotechnology, academic, government, environmental and industrial customers and to clinical laboratories. Specialty Diagnostics offers clinical diagnostics, immunodiagnostics, microbiology and transplant diagnostics products and a healthcare market channel. Laboratory Products and Biopharma Services covers laboratory products, the research and safety market channel, and pharma services and clinical research. The company's brands include Thermo Scientific, Applied Biosystems, Invitrogen, Gibco, Fisher Scientific, Unity Lab Services, Patheon and PPD, and it serves pharmaceutical and biotech, academic and government, industrial and applied, and healthcare and diagnostics markets. FY25 revenue was $44.6 billion.

thesis.label: HOLD
thesis.body: Thermo Fisher's operations are improving, but the price already reflects much of that. Second-quarter organic growth of 5% was above the six-month rate of 3%, management reports customer activity strengthening across its end markets, and productivity lifted the income margin of every segment. Against that, acquisitions supplied half of the quarter's reported growth, academic-and-government and diagnostics revenue were flat for the half, and the shares have climbed to the top of their 52-week range. At 26.2x the FY26 consensus, the multiple leaves room for the consensus earnings path and little more. We rate the shares HOLD.

catalysts: Organic follow-through: a second half that holds the second quarter's organic pace, rather than slipping back to the six-month rate, would support the Bull case.
Portfolio reshaping: the Clario acquisition (March 24, 2026) and the microbiology divestiture announced in the second quarter change the mix of two segments.
Productivity: further PPI-driven margin gains would let earnings grow faster than revenue, as they did in the second quarter.
Buybacks: the company repurchased $1.0 billion of stock in the second quarter, and the diluted share count fell year over year.
risks: Valuation: the shares trade near their 52-week high and above the consensus target, so a de-rating would hurt even if estimates are met.
Funding exposure: academic and government customers depend on budgets, and the October 2025 federal shutdown shows how an impasse can delay spending.
Acquisition reliance: deals supplied much of the recent reported growth, so weaker organic demand or a pause in dealmaking would show quickly in the top line.
Leverage: trailing net debt is 3.5x EBITDA, which narrows room for another large debt-funded deal.
Leadership change: the CFO, president and COO roles changed hands in early 2026, and two executive vice presidents left.

income.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31; Q2 ended June 27, 2026.

financials.incomeCommentary:
Second-quarter revenue was $11,994 million, up 10% year over year from $10,855 million; six-month revenue was $22,999 million, up 8%. Organic growth was {+5%+} in the quarter and {+3%+} for the half, with acquisitions adding 5 points and 4 points and currency 1 point and 2 points. Half of the quarter's reported growth therefore came from deals: Clario, acquired on March 24, 2026, and the filtration and separation business bought from Solventum on September 1, 2025. GAAP operating income rose {+14% to $2,087 million+} and GAAP operating margin rose {+0.5 point to 17.4%+}; adjusted operating margin was 22.8%, up 0.9 point. The company credits strong productivity improvements, offset in part by unfavorable business mix. GAAP diluted EPS rose {+9% to $4.68+} and adjusted EPS rose {+13% to $6.03+}; the main reconciling item is $1.31 per share of acquisition-related intangible amortization. Diluted shares fell to 371 million from 378 million.

Segment figures are gross of $565 million of eliminations. Life Sciences Solutions revenue rose 13% to $2,815 million, but only 3% was organic, with acquisitions adding 9 points; its income margin was 37.0%. Analytical Instruments rose 7%, all organic, to $1,847 million, and its income margin rose {+4.2 points to 23.0%+} on productivity, volume leverage and currency. Specialty Diagnostics rose 6% to $1,205 million at a 27.7% margin. Laboratory Products and Biopharma Services rose 12% to $6,693 million at a 14.0% margin, with clinical research up $441 million, primarily from Clario. The annual tables on this page show a single reportable segment; the 10-Q reports four, and we follow the 10-Q.

The annual record is less steady. FY25 revenue of $44.6 billion grew 3.9% after a flat FY24 and a 4.6% decline in FY23, FY25 operating margin, at the same level as the quarter's GAAP margin, compares with 25.6% in FY21, and FY25 diluted EPS of $17.74 remains below FY21's $19.46.

balance.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31; Q2 ended June 27, 2026.

financials.balanceCommentary: Debt rose in FY25, but much of the increase sat in cash at year-end. Total debt was $39.4 billion at FY25, up from $31.3 billion at FY24, while cash and short-term investments rose to $10.1 billion from $5.6 billion, so net debt rose by less, to $29.5 billion from $27.3 billion. On a trailing basis, net debt is 3.5x EBITDA. That is higher than FY25 year-end net debt against FY25 EBITDA of $10.5 billion would give; the page does not show the mid-2026 balance sheet or how the March 2026 Clario purchase was paid for, so we do not attribute the difference. Interest coverage is 5.6x on a trailing basis. Second-quarter interest expense was $401 million against $404 million a year earlier, but interest income fell to $207 million from $297 million, so the net cost of financing rose; for the six months, interest expense was $755 million against $707 million. Total equity grew to $53.4 billion from $49.6 billion, and the current ratio was 1.89 at FY25 and 1.55 on a trailing basis. Coverage at that level makes the debt serviceable, but at this leverage there is less room for another large debt-funded acquisition without leaning further on cash flow.

cashflow.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31; Q2 ended June 27, 2026.

financials.cashflowCommentary: Free cash flow fell in FY25 and was stronger in the second quarter of 2026. Operating cash flow was $7.8 billion in FY25, down from $8.7 billion, and free cash flow was $6.3 billion against $7.3 billion, taking FCF margin to 14.1% from 16.9%; FY25 free cash flow was the lowest of the five years shown, and the page gives no reason for the decline. Capital expenditure fell from $2.5 billion in FY21 to $1.5 billion in FY25. In the second quarter, operating cash flow was $2,125 million against $1,399 million a year earlier, and free cash flow was $1,678 million against $1,105 million after $450 million of property, plant and equipment purchases, up from $294 million. One quarter does not show that the FY25 decline has reversed. Capital return runs mainly through buybacks: the company repurchased $3.0 billion of stock and paid $0.6 billion of dividends in FY25, both covered by free cash flow, and the dividend yield is 0.29%. The trailing FCF yield is 3.0%.

multiples.note: Peer multiples pending a peer data source.

valuation.multiplesCommentary: Thermo Fisher trades at 35.4x trailing earnings, 5.3x sales and 25.4x trailing EV/EBITDA. The forward multiples are much lower: 26.2x on the figure labelled next-twelve-month earnings and about 23.9x the FY27 consensus EPS. That figure lines up with the FY26 consensus EPS of $25.13, so we treat it as a current-year multiple. Most of the gap between the trailing and forward multiples is a difference in earnings basis rather than growth. The trailing multiple is consistent with GAAP earnings, such as FY25 diluted EPS of $17.74, while the consensus estimates sit near the company's adjusted earnings, which were $11.47 per share for the six months against GAAP EPS of $9.10; the page does not label the estimates' basis. We therefore value the shares only on forward multiples of forward estimates, and the reference is today's forward multiple. The FY27 consensus of $27.54 implies earnings growth in the high single digits over FY26. The Street is positive on the rating but not on the price: 24 of 29 analysts rate the shares Buy, yet the consensus target of $649.96 and the median of $650.00 sit below the current price, within a range of $520.00 to $780.00. The page carries no peer multiples, so the comparison is with the company's own forward earnings and the Street's targets.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: The second quarter's 5% organic growth proves a floor, instruments and bioproduction keep growing, and productivity keeps lifting margins. EPS reaches the FY27 consensus of $27.54 with momentum beyond it, and the multiple rises to a little over twenty-eight times, about two turns above today's 26.2x forward, giving $780.00, the Street's high target. Against it: this needs a re-rating on top of the rise from the 52-week low, and no Street target sits higher.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: Organic growth holds in the mid-single digits, acquisitions add to reported growth, and EPS reaches the same FY27 consensus. The multiple eases to about twenty-five times, about one turn below today's forward multiple, giving $688.50. For holding today's multiple: the second quarter accelerated and every segment's margin rose. Against it: organic growth for the half was 3%, the price sits at the top of its range and the consensus target is below it. The modest step down is our judgment.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: Organic growth falls back to or below the six-month pace: a funding impasse like October 2025 hits academic and government customers, already flat for the half, and pharma demand cools. Deals and productivity hold EPS near the FY26 consensus of $25.13 with no growth in FY27, and the multiple falls to about twenty-one times, five turns below today's forward multiple, giving $520.00, the Street's low target. The shares traded at $435.27 within the year, so this is not extreme; margin gains argue against pricing it lower.

valuation.scenarioCommentary: We weight the Bull at 25%, the Base at 50% and the Bear at 25%. The probability-weighted value is $669.25 against a price of $658.92, so expected upside is roughly flat, and the Bear sits about a fifth below the price. All three scenarios use one framework: a multiple of FY27 earnings a year out, compared with today's forward multiple. The Bear weight rests on evidence on both sides. For a higher weight: organic growth was 3% for the half, academic-and-government and diagnostics revenue were flat over the six months, the October 2025 shutdown shows how funding can stall, and the shares have risen to the top of their 52-week range. For a lower weight: second-quarter organic growth was 5%, sales rose in every major geography, management reports strengthening customer activity, and every segment's margin rose. We judge those balanced and set the Bull and Bear weights equal. The Base anchor is the main judgment in the report. Holding today's forward multiple on FY27 consensus would lift the Base by about one turn of earnings, and anchoring it to the consensus target would lower it; at these weights, either still derives HOLD, so the anchor does not decide the label. The call is not close to the BUY or SELL line.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: The company reports four segments, and the economics differ widely. Life Sciences Solutions, built on reagents, consumables and bioproduction, earned a 37.0% segment income margin in the second quarter. Laboratory Products and Biopharma Services, which brings in more revenue than the other three and is home to the research and safety market channel, pharma services and clinical research, earned 14.0%. Analytical Instruments and Specialty Diagnostics sit between the two at 23.0% and 27.7%. The mix spans consumables, instruments, diagnostics and services sold to pharmaceutical and biotech, academic and government, industrial and applied, and healthcare customers, which spreads demand across end markets with different cycles.

moatFactors.name: Scale and breadth
moatFactors.body: FY25 revenue of $44.6 billion spans four segments and brands from Thermo Scientific and Applied Biosystems to Fisher Scientific, Patheon and PPD, letting the company sell across a customer's research, production and clinical work. The limit: breadth has not prevented swings in the annual record, including the FY23 revenue decline.

moatFactors.name: Embedded workflows and consumables
moatFactors.body: Reagents, consumables and services are used inside customers' research and production workflows, which makes repeat purchasing likely once instruments and processes are in place. The consumables-heavy Life Sciences Solutions segment earns more per dollar of revenue than the other segments. The page does not quantify the recurring share of revenue, so this rests on the business description and segment margins.

moatFactors.name: Commercial channels
moatFactors.body: The research and safety market channel and the healthcare market channel give the company direct reach to laboratories and healthcare customers, and management cites continued share gain. The channel business runs at a lower margin, inside the lower-margin Laboratory Products and Biopharma Services segment, so its advantage is reach rather than pricing.

moatFactors.name: PPI productivity system
moatFactors.body: The company credits its PPI Business System, covering price realization, sourcing, restructuring and low-cost manufacturing, for margin gains in every segment in the second quarter. It is a repeatable operating discipline, but it lifts margins rather than protecting demand.

businessMoat.durability: The moat rests on structure rather than one product cycle: four segments, several end markets and a consumables and services base that is used inside customers' workflows. In the six months to June 27, 2026, academic-and-government and diagnostics revenue were flat while pharma and biotech grew strongly, which shows the spread working. The threats are cyclical capital spending by customers, dependence on government funding, and reliance on acquisitions for a large part of growth, which adds integration risk. FY25 operating margin of 17.4% stays well below FY21's 25.6%, so the moat has not protected peak profitability. We rate the moat WIDE on scale, breadth and workflow embedding, with the caveat that the page carries no return-on-capital figure to test it against.

points: Consensus expects revenue to rise from $44.6 billion in FY25 to about $47.9 billion in FY26 (+7%) and $50.3 billion in FY27, with EPS of $25.13 and $27.54. The page does not split the FY26 revenue growth between acquisitions and organic growth, and the Clario and filtration deals are part of it.

Acquisitions are a large growth source. Clario drove most of the $441 million rise in clinical research revenue in the second quarter, and the filtration and separation business added to the $196 million rise in bioproduction. The filtration deal closed on September 1, 2025, so its contribution enters the year-over-year comparison from September 2026.

Organic growth improved to 5% in the second quarter from 3% for the half, led by Laboratory Products and Biopharma Services and Analytical Instruments, where electron microscopy rose $55 million. One quarter of acceleration is not yet a trend.

Productivity adds to earnings growth beyond revenue: adjusted EPS grew 13% in the second quarter against 10% revenue growth. The company also cites unfavorable business mix and strategic investments as partial offsets.

New products support the instrument business, including the Thermo Scientific Orbitrap Tribrid Apex and Orbitrap Excedion mass spectrometers and the Applied Biosystems PowerFlex Thermal Cycler launched in the quarter. The page gives no revenue figure for them.

management.leadership: According to the 2026 proxy statement (filed April 7, 2026), Marc N. Casper became Chairman and Chief Executive Officer effective March 1, 2026, having held the titles of Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer in 2025, and Gianluca Pettiti was promoted to President and Chief Operating Officer. James R. Meyer succeeded Stephen Williamson as Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer as of March 1, 2026, and Mr. Williamson retired effective March 31, 2026. Michel Lagarde, Executive Vice President and Chief Operating Officer in 2025, left the company as of March 31, 2026, and Frederick Lowery, an Executive Vice President, left as of February 28, 2026. That is a lot of senior change in a short window. Mr. Casper's continuity as chief executive and the internal promotion of Mr. Pettiti reduce the risk, and the second-quarter results came after the changes took effect.
management.capitalAllocation: Capital goes first to acquisitions and buybacks; dividends are small. The September 2025 purchase of the filtration and separation business from Solventum added bioproduction capacity, the March 2026 Clario deal added clinical research, and the company announced the divestiture of its microbiology business in the second quarter, so it is pruning as well as buying. Buybacks, set out in the cash-flow review, continued in the second quarter. The acquisition program has lifted debt, so the discipline to judge is whether deals earn their cost while leverage stays at a level the cash flow covers. The page gives no return figures for the deals.
management.governance: From the 2026 proxy statement (filed April 7, 2026): the Corporate Governance Guidelines require that a majority of directors and every member of the Audit, Compensation and N&CG committees be independent. The Board determined that 10 directors qualify as independent and that each member of those committees is independent, and it considers tenure in its independence review for directors with more than nine years of service. Mr. Casper combines the chairman and chief executive roles. The compensation program is described as performance-based, shareholder-aligned and market-competitive, with stock ownership guidelines, a clawback policy and a stock holding requirement for the CEO. The excerpt does not cover related-party transactions, so we draw no conclusion on them.
management.insiderOwnership: As of February 28, 2026, all current directors and executive officers as a group (19 individuals) beneficially owned 1,207,932 shares, less than one percent of the stock, according to the 2026 proxy statement. Mr. Casper's 449,661 shares include 323,471 shares under options exercisable on or before April 28, 2026 and 9,411 restricted stock units vesting by that date. The 5% holders listed are The Vanguard Group at 8.87% and BlackRock, Inc. at 7.62%, but both figures come from filings made in February 2024 and are dated; Vanguard's most recent Schedule 13G/A, filed March 27, 2026, reported 0.0% after an internal reorganization that disaggregated its reporting. For outside holders, insider stakes are too small to matter for control, so alignment rests on the ownership guidelines and pay design.

idiosyncratic: Acquisition reliance: acquisitions contributed 5 of the second quarter's 10 points of reported growth and 4 of the half's 8 points. Clario and the filtration business are still being integrated, and once they enter the year-over-year base, reported growth depends on organic demand or new deals.

Leadership turnover: the CFO, president and COO roles changed and two executive vice presidents left in early 2026, as set out in the management section. Execution risk is higher than usual while the new team settles.
Valuation: the shares sit near the 52-week high and above the Street's consensus and median targets, so a de-rating would cut the price even if earnings meet consensus; the Bear case prices this.
Leverage: the debt described in the balance-sheet review narrows the room for further debt-funded deals, and a fall in cash generation like FY25's would tighten it.

Microbiology divestiture: the sale announced in the second quarter will remove a business from Specialty Diagnostics; the page gives no price or revenue for it, so its effect on growth and margins is unknown.
risks.systemic: The company's FY2025 10-K (filed February 26, 2026) flags that its served markets can experience cyclical downturns and that general economic conditions, including inflation it describes as elevated, affect demand, order cancellations and pricing. International operations expose results to currency, which added $0.37 billion to 2025 revenue and can reverse, and to tariffs, trade measures and Chinese regulations that favor local suppliers. Customer capital spending and government funding policies are a direct channel: the October 2025 federal shutdown is the example the company itself gives. Public health emergencies have disrupted operations and supply in the past and may again. None of this is unique to Thermo Fisher, but its scale and international footprint mean a broad economic or trade shock would show in reported results.

body: Thermo Fisher Scientific is a HOLD around a Base of $688.50. The business is doing well: organic growth reached 5% in the second quarter, margins rose in every segment and adjusted EPS grew faster than revenue. The price already reflects that. The shares sit at the top of their 52-week range, above the consensus target, and our probability-weighted value of $669.25 is close to today's price, while the Bear at $520.00 sits about a fifth below it.

The target range is the band in which our scenarios derive HOLD. Below the $605 target low, the same scenarios derive BUY; above the $705 target high, which is also above the 52-week high of $671.47, they derive SELL. Neither is met today. The shares rose from a 52-week low of $435.27, and no source on the page explains the move; closes in the lower part of that range sat below the target low, where these scenarios would have derived BUY. The label is HOLD because of where the price stands now.
